meta.title: TRAINING PROGRAM - 12 MONTHS
meta.subtitle: 52-week plan in four phases, built for 6 training days per week at about 60 minutes per session (a few short second sessions are marked as optional or PM add-ons). A full year is the right runway: it buys a real muscle-building block up front and a long, gradual endurance ramp that keeps you healthy.

overview.heading: 52-week plan in four phases, built for 6 training days per week at about 60 minutes per session (a few short second sessions are marked as optional or PM add-ons). A full year is the right runway: it buys a real muscle-building block up front and a long, gradual endurance ramp that keeps you healthy.

entries.label: Phase 1 - Foundation (Months 1-3, Wk 1-12)
entries.text: Muscle gain is the priority: this is where most of your 10-20 lb goal gets built. Hypertrophy lifting, short easy runs, light rucks. Boring on purpose; do not rush it.

entries.label: Phase 2 - Strength (Months 4-6, Wk 13-24)
entries.text: Main lifts go heavy (5x5, weighted pull-ups), running intervals begin, rucks build to 6 miles at 40 lb.

entries.label: Phase 3 - Engine (Months 7-9, Wk 25-36)
entries.text: Endurance takes the lead: mileage peaks near 28/week, threshold running, rucks to 8-9 miles at 45 lb, monthly Saturday long rucks. Strength shifts to heavy-but-brief maintenance. Week 36: 2-mile time trial.

entries.label: Phase 4 - Peak & Taper (Months 10-12, Wk 37-52)
entries.text: event-specific: two rucks per week, event-style carries under fatigue, 12-mile ruck assessments at Weeks 44 and 49, then a 3-week taper (Wk 50-52) so you arrive fresh.

entries.label: Monday
entries.text: Lower body strength (full-body maintenance in Phase 4). PM: 15 min mobility.

entries.label: Tuesday
entries.text: Run (easy in Phase 1, intervals after) + pull-up maintenance.

entries.label: Wednesday
entries.text: Upper body strength. Phase 4 swaps this day to the midweek ruck.

entries.label: Thursday
entries.text: Ruck (Phases 1-3). Phase 4: easy run + light upper body.

entries.label: Friday
entries.text: Full-body work capacity: kettlebell work, loaded carries, rower intervals, incline hikes.

entries.label: Saturday
entries.text: Long run. Monthly long ruck in Phase 3; alternating long ruck/run in Phase 4.

entries.label: Sunday
entries.text: Full rest + 30 min flexibility session (Mobility & Flexibility tab).

entries.label: Lifting
entries.text: When you hit the top of the rep range on every set with good form, add 5 lb (upper body) or 10 lb (lower body) next session. Leave 1-3 reps in the tank on every set. Grinding maximal reps is how you get hurt.

entries.label: Running
entries.text: Weekly mileage climbs roughly 10% per week with a deload every 4th week. Easy runs must be conversational. Exact weekly targets: Run & Ruck Progression tab.

entries.label: Rucking
entries.text: Start at 25 lb dry (without water and food), add roughly 5 lb every month, cap at 55 lb. Never add distance and weight in the same week. Walk fast (goal under 15 min/mile); shuffle-jogging flats is allowed from Phase 2 if joints tolerate it.

entries.label: Flexibility
entries.text: 10 minutes daily after training plus the Sunday session. Consistency beats duration.

overview.heading: INJURY GUARDRAILS BUILT INTO THIS PLAN

entries.label: Back
entries.text: Trap-bar deadlift instead of conventional; chest-supported and braced rows; anti-extension and anti-rotation core work (planks, Pallof press) rather than sit-up volume.

entries.label: Shoulders
entries.text: Landmine and neutral-grip pressing instead of straight barbell overhead work; face pulls and band pull-aparts every upper day. If a press hurts, lower the incline or go single-arm.

entries.label: Knees, ankles, hips
entries.text: A year-long gradual volume ramp with deloads every 4th week; rucks start light and short; calf and ankle work weekly. Sharp joint pain means stop the session, not push through it.

entries.label: Week 36
entries.text: 2-mile time trial. Target sub-14:00.

entries.label: Week 44
entries.text: 12-mile ruck at 45 lb dry. Target sub-3:15. A rehearsal, not a max effort.

entries.label: Week 49
entries.text: 12-mile ruck at 45 lb dry. Target sub-3:00, goal 2:45. Your green light for selection.

entries.label: Weeks 50-52
entries.text: Taper. Volume drops ~40-60%. Fitness is already built; the taper lets it show up on day one.

entries.label: Feet
entries.text: Break in the boots you will wear at selection during every ruck, all year. Tape hot spots early. Foot failure ends more selection attempts than fitness does.

entries.label: Sleep
entries.text: 7-9 hours. You cannot out-train a sleep deficit at this volume.

entries.label: Food
entries.text: See the Nutrition tabs. Calorie surplus through Phase 2, performance-first from Phase 3 on.

entries.label: Missed days
entries.text: Skip it and continue the plan as written. Never stack two missed sessions into one day.

phases.name: PHASE 1 - FOUNDATION & MUSCLE: WEEKS 1-12
phases.description: Priority: muscle gain and aerobic base. Deload every 4th week (Wk 4, 8, 12): drop a set from each lift, cut run mileage ~25%, keep the ruck short.

days.title: LOWER BODY STRENGTH
days.notes: Hypertrophy block: RPE 7, full range, controlled lowering. Add 10 lb when all sets are clean. This phase is where the muscle gets built.

days.title: EASY RUN + PULL-UP MAINTENANCE
days.notes: Conversational pace; walk breaks fine the first month. From Wk 9, finish runs with 4 x 20-sec relaxed strides. Band-assist pull-ups if under 5 reps.

days.title: UPPER BODY STRENGTH
days.notes: Neutral-grip and landmine pressing protect the shoulders. Face pulls every upper day, no exceptions. Arm work is for mass; drop it first if short on time.

days.title: RUCK
days.notes: Brisk walk only, mostly flat. Wear the boots you'll take to selection, starting now. Tape hot spots the moment they appear.

days.title: FULL-BODY CONDITIONING
days.notes: Circuit style, 60-90 sec rests. KB swings are a hinge, not a squat: hips snap, arms just hold on. The incline hike is ruck-legs without the ruck.

days.title: LONG RUN
days.notes: Entirely conversational. This builds the aerobic base everything at selection sits on.

days.title: REST + FLEXIBILITY
days.notes: Complete rest otherwise. The adaptation happens today. Stretch to mild tension, never pain.

phases.name: PHASE 2 - STRENGTH: WEEKS 13-24
phases.description: Priority: heavy strength on the muscle built in Phase 1; intervals begin. Deload every 4th week.

days.title: LOWER BODY STRENGTH

items.name: Nordic curl or heavy leg curl

days.notes: Main lifts at RPE 8. Work to a top set of 5 on trap-bar; add 10 lb when all fives are crisp. Front-loaded squatting spares the lower back.

days.title: RUN INTERVALS + PULL-UPS
days.notes: Intervals are where the speed comes from; even pacing beats a fast first rep. Extend the pyramid peak as you get stronger. Deload weeks: easy running only.

days.title: UPPER BODY STRENGTH
days.notes: Weighted pull-ups are the highest-value upper lift for selection. No straps on carries; grip is a limiter at selection. Skip the PM run if joints are cranky.

days.title: RUCK
days.notes: Target pace under 15 min/mile. Shuffle-jog flats if joints tolerate it. Add moderate hills from Wk 17. Never add distance and weight the same week.

days.title: WORK CAPACITY
days.notes: EMOM = every minute on the minute; quality reps under fatigue. Step-ups carry straight over to rucking hills.

days.title: LONG RUN
days.notes: Last 10 minutes at moderate (not hard) effort, except deload weeks.

days.title: REST + FLEXIBILITY
days.notes: Deloads Wk 16 and 20 and 24: cut mileage ~25%, drop a set from each lift, keep the ruck short.

phases.name: PHASE 3 - ENGINE: WEEKS 25-36
phases.description: Priority: endurance. Mileage peaks near 28/week, rucks reach 9 miles, strength holds on brief heavy work. Week 36: 2-mile time trial.

days.title: LOWER BODY STRENGTH
days.notes: Heavy but brief: strength holds on lower volume while the endurance work grows. Nothing to failure.

days.title: RUN INTERVALS + PULL-UPS
days.notes: Threshold = comfortably hard, about the pace you could hold for an hour race. The time trial is a benchmark, not a race; run it fresh after a deload.

days.title: UPPER BODY STRENGTH
days.notes: The optional PM run adds aerobic volume cheaply; take it most weeks in this phase unless joints complain.

days.title: RUCK

items.raw: Hills every week from here on

days.notes: Pace under 15 min/mile on rolling terrain. Deload weeks: 5 mi at 35 lb.

days.title: WORK CAPACITY
days.notes: Front-rack carries brace the trunk the way awkward team-event loads do. Vest hike at 25-35 lb; it's extra ruck-legs without extra foot pounding.

days.title: LONG RUN / MONTHLY LONG RUCK
days.notes: The monthly Saturday long ruck starts rehearsing Phase 4. Full foot care after every event.

days.title: REST + FLEXIBILITY
days.notes: Deloads Wk 28, 32, 36 (run mileage only; those weeks' Saturday rucks stay). If you feel run down two weeks straight, take a full extra rest day.

phases.name: PHASE 4 - PEAK AND TAPER: WEEKS 37-52
phases.description: Priority: event-specific readiness. Two rucks per week, assessments Wk 44 and 49, 3-week taper Wk 50-52.

days.title: FULL-BODY STRENGTH (MAINTENANCE)
days.notes: Maintain, don't chase PRs in the final months. Bodyweight pull-ups only in Weeks 50-52.

days.title: RUN INTERVALS + PULL-UPS
days.notes: Nothing to failure after Week 48. Taper weeks keep the legs quick without digging a hole.

days.title: MIDWEEK RUCK
days.notes: Short but heavy. Never exceed 55 lb dry in training; heavier grinds joints and teaches bad movement before selection.

days.title: EASY RUN + LIGHT UPPER
days.notes: Recovery pace between hard days. The gym work here is light pump volume, well short of failure.

days.title: EVENT SIMULATION / WORK CAPACITY
days.notes: Heavy carries under fatigue simulate team events and log PT. Weeks 50-52: cut to 2 light rounds of carries only. Taper means taper.

exercises.notes: Hip flexors take a beating from rucking and running.

exercises.notes: Slight knee bend, hinge from the hips.

exercises.notes: Both versions hit gastroc and soleus. Ankle mobility protects the knees on rucks.

exercises.notes: Counters pressing volume; helps shoulder health.

exercises.notes: Gentle spinal movement, especially after deadlift days.

overview.heading: Built for: 160 lb, 5'11", 6 training days/week with climbing run and ruck volume. Dinners are excluded (you plan those with your partner); this plan covers everything else and tells you what dinner needs to contribute.

entries.label: Training days (Mon-Sat)
entries.text: 3,300-3,500 kcal. Protein 160 g minimum. Carbs 380-450 g (fuel for the running and rucking). Fat 90-110 g. The meal plan tab covers ~2,770 kcal and ~180 g protein at the default options; dinner needs to add roughly 550-750 kcal, and protein is already covered before dinner.

entries.label: Rest day (Sunday)
entries.text: 2,800-3,000 kcal. Skip the pre- and post-workout entries; everything else stays the same. Keep protein at 160 g; recovery is when the muscle actually gets built.

entries.label: Taper (Wk 50-52)
entries.text: Drop to roughly maintenance (2,900-3,100) as training volume falls in the final three weeks. Do not show up at selection mid-bulk; show up light, fueled, and fast.

overview.heading: THE ADJUSTMENT RULE (this is the whole system)

entries.label: Weigh-in protocol
entries.text: Weigh yourself every morning after the bathroom, before food, and take the weekly average. Log it in the Training Log tab.

entries.label: If the average is flat 2 weeks
entries.text: Add 200 kcal/day (easiest: 1 extra tbsp peanut butter and 1 cup of milk).

entries.label: If gaining over 1 lb/week
entries.text: Subtract 200 kcal/day. Faster than 1 lb/week at your size is mostly fat.

entries.label: Creatine monohydrate
entries.text: 5 g every day, training or not. Timing doesn't matter; consistency does. Mix it into the post-workout shake or morning drink. No loading phase needed; it saturates in 3-4 weeks. Expect 2-4 lb of quick water weight in muscle: that's normal and useful. Drink more water and it plays fine with ruck training.

entries.label: Whey protein
entries.text: 1-2 scoops/day as written in the meal plan. It's food in convenient form, nothing magic. Any third-party tested brand (NSF Certified for Sport or Informed Sport) is fine.

entries.label: Skip everything else
entries.text: Pre-workouts, mass gainers, BCAAs: not worth the money at your stage. Caffeine before hard sessions is effective; since you don't drink coffee, 100-200 mg via caffeine pill or a sugar-free energy drink does the same job.

entries.label: Over 75 minutes
entries.text: 30-60 g carbs per hour during: gels, chews, dried fruit, or a sports drink. Practice this on training rucks; selection is fueled the same way and race-day-new food is how you end up sick on a ruck.

entries.label: Hydration + sodium
entries.text: Half your bodyweight in oz of water daily as a floor (~80 oz), more on ruck days. For rucks over 90 min or hot days, add electrolytes (500-700 mg sodium/hour). Salty sweater signs: white crust on your hat, cramping.

entries.label: Post-session window
entries.text: Within about an hour of hard sessions: 30-40 g protein + 60-100 g carbs. The post-workout shake in the plan handles it.

entries.label: PM sessions
entries.text: On days with a PM run or mobility work, no extra meal is needed; the plan's snacks already cover it. If a PM run leaves you hollow, add a glass of milk before bed.
